title: Free-bar skeletal cells and terminal augmentation contraction data
statement:
Use small simplicial sets and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and projective structures of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category and $Z:C\to\mathsf{sSet}$ any functor. Define the free $C$-diagram $F_cK(d)=\operatorname{Hom}_C(c,d)\times K$. For $k\geq0$ set
$$P_k(d)=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_k\to d}Z(c_0).$$
Faces compose adjacent arrows, the first face applies $Z(c_0\to c_1)$, and degeneracies insert identity arrows among $c_0,\ldots,c_k$. Write $QZ=\int^{[k]}P_k\times\Delta^k$, the objectwise quotient by the simplex-operator relations; equivalently $(QZ(d))_r=(P_r(d))_r$. There is a natural filtration $\varnothing=Q_{-1}Z\to Q_0Z\to Q_1Z\to\cdots$ with colimit $QZ$, where $Q_kZ$ is the image of outer simplices of dimension at most $k$. For every $k\geq0$, the map $Q_{k-1}Z\to Q_kZ$ is the pushout in $C$-diagrams of the coproduct, over strings $c_0\to\cdots\to c_k$ with every displayed arrow nonidentity, of
$$F_{c_k}(Z(c_0)\times\partial\Delta^k)\longrightarrow F_{c_k}(Z(c_0)\times\Delta^k).$$
The attaching maps are induced by the stated faces. In particular $QZ$ is projectively cofibrant. Composition gives an augmentation $P_\bullet(d)\to\operatorname{const}Z(d)$. On each set of inner $r$-simplices it has terminal extra-degeneracy maps $h_k$, obtained by appending $d$ and $1_d$ to the string ending in $d$, and $h_{-1}(z)=(d,1_d,z)$. They satisfy $\varepsilon h_{-1}=1$, $d_{k+1}h_k=1$, $d_0h_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon$, $d_i h_k=h_{k-1}d_i$ for $k\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq k$, and $s_i h_k=h_{k+1}s_i$ for $0\leq i\leq k$; the operations commute with the inner simplicial operators. All data, including augmentation, are natural in $Z$. No fibrancy or nonemptiness is assumed.

proof.text: Write $P_k=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_k}F_{c_k}Z(c_0)$. For a monotone map $\alpha:[m]\to[k]$, restrict a string to $c_{\alpha(0)},\ldots,c_{\alpha(m)}$, compose the intervening arrows and the terminal arrow to $d$, and apply $Z(c_0\to c_{\alpha(0)})$ to its value. Associativity and functoriality identify restriction by $\alpha\beta$ with restriction first by $\alpha$ and then by $\beta$; identity restriction is the identity. These formulas give exactly the faces and degeneracies in the statement, including the last face composing $c_{k-1}\to c_k\to d$. They commute with inner simplicial operators. Degreewise the coend has representatives $(x,\alpha)$ with $x\in P_k(d)_r$ and $\alpha:[r]\to[k]$. The map $[x,\alpha]\mapsto P(\alpha)(x)$ to $P_r(d)_r$ respects its defining relations; its inverse sends $y$ to $[y,1_{[r]}]$, since the coend relation gives $[x,\alpha]=[P(\alpha)x,1_{[r]}]$. These inverse formulas commute with the diagonal operators. Postcomposition of the terminal arrow gives the $C$-diagram structure, and a natural transformation of $Z$ commutes with each formula. All index sets are small under the cited conventions.

source.place: §7, printed p.13, displayed replacement over strings ending at i. Agent expansion of its operators and degreewise coend identification.

proof.text: Define $N_k(d)\subseteq P_k(d)$ as the union of the summands indexed by strings whose internal arrows $c_0\to\cdots\to c_k$ are all nonidentity, with any terminal arrow to $d$, and $D_k(d)$ as the complementary union. Inner operators, postcomposition in $d$ and maps of $Z$ do not change the internal string, so both are sub-$C$-diagrams. Fix $d$ and an inner degree $r$ and let $T=P_\bullet(d)_r$, an outer simplicial set [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. An outer $k$-simplex is degenerate exactly when it lies in $D_k(d)_r$: the image of $s_i$ has $c_i\to c_{i+1}$ an identity; conversely, if $c_i\to c_{i+1}$ is $1$ with $0\leq i<k$, then $d_{i+1}$ composes it with the next arrow (the terminal arrow if $i+1=k$) leaving the value unchanged, and $s_i$ reinserts it, so $x=s_id_{i+1}x$. Colimits of $C$-diagrams of simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] are formed objectwise and degreewise in sets, so $(L_kP)(d)_r=L_kT$ for the proper-surjection latching colimit, with the same structure maps. By [lem-coef-simplicial-latching-degenerate-subset], $\lambda_k:L_kT\to T_k$ is injective with image the degenerate subset $D_k(d)_r$, naturally in $T$. Inner operators, postcomposition in $d$ and maps of $Z$ are maps of these outer simplicial sets, so this naturality shows that $\lambda_k:L_kP\to P_k$ is an isomorphism of $C$-diagrams of simplicial sets onto $D_k$. Hence $P_k\cong L_kP\amalg N_k$ compatibly with $\lambda_k$, naturally in $Z$, with no condition on the terminal arrow or the inner simplex. For $k=0$ there are no internal arrows and $L_0P=D_0=\varnothing$.

proof.text: Let $R_k(P)$ be the truncated coend with outer indices at most $k$, and set $R_{-1}(P)=\varnothing$. For fixed $d,r$, apply [lem-coef-truncated-coend-skeleton-image] to the outer simplicial set $S_n=P_n(d)_r$. Its map sends $[x,\alpha]$ to $P(\alpha)x$ and is injective with image the outer simplices generated in dimensions at most $k$. By the coend/diagonal formula of step 1 this is precisely the specified image $Q_kZ(d)_r$. Naturality of this comparison in $S$ makes it commute with inner operators, postcomposition in $d$, and maps of $Z$. Hence $R_k(P)\cong Q_kZ$ with their specified maps into $QZ$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-tensor-coend-skeletal-pushouts] to the outer simplicial object $P$ in the category of $C$-diagrams of simplicial sets, using its objectwise Cartesian tensor and small colimits; this is the projective simplicial presheaf category of [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model] with $D=C^{\mathrm{op}}$. The cited theorem gives the latching/boundary pushout for $R_{k-1}(P)\to R_k(P)$, with the prescribed face maps, and colimit $QZ$. Use the preceding comparison to identify these stages with $Q_{k-1}Z$ and $Q_kZ$. All required index categories are small; no cofibrancy hypothesis is used for this pushout.

proof.text: Substitute $P_k=L_kP\amalg N_k$ into that square. Products distribute over these disjoint unions degreewise, so its attaching object is $(L_kP\times\Delta^k)\amalg(N_k\times\partial\Delta^k)$ and its disk object is $(L_kP\times\Delta^k)\amalg(N_k\times\Delta^k)$. In the pushout universal property the identical $L_kP\times\Delta^k$ summand cancels: a map on the disk object is already fixed there by the old-stage map. Thus the same square attaches $N_k\times\partial\Delta^k\to N_k\times\Delta^k$. Since $N_k=\coprod_{c_0\to\cdots\to c_k\text{ nonidentity}}F_{c_k}Z(c_0)$, distributing again gives exactly the displayed free cells. Their boundary maps are the faces specified by the preceding theorem. At $k=0$, the latching object and boundary are empty. The cited colimit and stage comparisons give the required filtration with colimit $QZ$.

proof.text: The coefficient-weighted boundary maps in the preceding step are projective cofibrations, although they need not be individual generating cofibrations. Indeed, $K\times\partial\Delta^k\hookrightarrow K\times\Delta^k$ is degreewise injective for every simplicial set $K$, so it is a Kan-model cofibration by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. For any diagram $X$, evaluation at $1_c$ gives $\operatorname{Nat}(F_cK,X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,X(c))$, with inverse sending $u:K\to X(c)$ to $(a:c\to d,z)\mapsto X(a)u(z)$. Hence a lifting square from $F_c$ of the coefficient-weighted boundary against an objectwise trivial fibration is the corresponding square against its component at $c$, and has a diagonal. The projective lifting characterization in [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model], applied with $D=C^{\mathrm{op}}$, therefore makes each free map a projective cofibration. The lifting property survives coproducts by choosing each diagonal and pushouts by their universal property. For the sequential composite, start at the initial stage and extend a lift over each successor using the attached maps; the compatible lifts induce a lift on the colimit. Thus $\varnothing\to QZ$ is a projective cofibration, as required.

source.place: Remark A.3.3.5, printed p.871, free-diagram projective cofibrations; the free/evaluation bijection and closure under attachments are written explicitly.

proof.text: For fixed $d$ and inner degree $r$, augment a string by applying $Z$ to its composite $c_0\to d$. Composition of strings shows that this commutes with every outer operator, and functoriality shows that it commutes with inner operators and postcomposition in $d$. Set $h_{-1}(z)=(d,1_d,z)$ and send $(c_0\to\cdots\to c_k\xrightarrow{a}d,z)$ under $h_k$ to $(c_0\to\cdots\to c_k\xrightarrow{a}d\xrightarrow{1_d}d,z)$. The last face composes $a$ with $1_d$, giving $d_{k+1}h_k=1$. At $k=0$, the first face applies $Z(a)$ and leaves the string $d\xrightarrow{1_d}d$, giving $d_0h_0=h_{-1}\varepsilon$. For $k\geq1$, the first face applies $Z(c_0\to c_1)$ on either side of $d_0h_k=h_{k-1}d_0$, and both sides retain the same appended $d$. For $1\leq i<k$ the face composes the same two internal arrows; for $i=k$ both sides have terminal composite $c_{k-1}\to c_k\to d$, followed by $1_d$. These give every stated remaining face identity. Inserting an identity at $c_i$ on either side gives $s_ih_k=h_{k+1}s_i$ for $0\leq i\leq k$. Also $\varepsilon h_{-1}=1$ by $Z(1_d)=1$. The $h$ maps leave the inner value unchanged, and the augmentation commutes with inner operators because $Z(a)$ is a simplicial map. Naturality in $Z$ follows respectively from leaving the value unchanged and the naturality square for $Z(a)$.
